analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations
key_insights: US equities were net sold for a third straight week (four of the last five). Single stocks saw the largest de-grossing since July. The desk reports about $20bn of TMT selling over two weeks, approaching the $23bn seen in July's AI unwind.

The S&P 500 fell under 50bps on the week and sits 2.5% below its highs, but hedge fund portfolios were hit hard. On Thursday all three major hedge fund cohorts (Fundamental L/S, Systematic, Multi-Strats) lost more than 1% on the same day for the first time since COVID. The GS Hedge Fund VIP long/short basket fell 4%.

Coppersmith reads the move as an investor leverage unwind, not an AI demand bubble bursting. Positioning has moved faster than fundamentals. Hedge fund gross leverage was still 312% (96th percentile over five years) while fundamental net leverage fell to 47%, a one-year low.

Pasquariello says risk/reward is still unclear and he has limited conviction. He notes the market has done a lot of work: de-risking across levered funds, firmer implied vol, cyclicals vs defensives hit hard, and the Risk Appetite Indicator turned negative for the first time since March. He says this is the kind of setup where odds often favor the bull.

The AI debate has shifted to the supply of power and capital for the buildout. Privorotsky says the cost of capital has repriced and hyperscaler and data center credit spreads have widened across the capital structure. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings this week are the test of how backlog converts to cloud revenue and how the next leg of capex is financed.

Privorotsky lays out hyperscaler capex scenarios. Worst case is capex accelerating funded by expensive debt, or capex cut because financing is unavailable. Best case is capex rising with accelerating organic cash flow and a path to self-funding through 2027/28. Middle case is flat or higher capex with more equity financing, which is bad for hyperscaler equity and potentially good for credit.

CTA positioning raises left-tail risk. Equity CTAs are long $38.5bn of S&P futures (91st percentile, nearly 80% of aggregate net longs). The S&P is already below the short-term trend threshold, and the medium-term level is about 1.3% below Friday's close. The model has CTAs selling $11.6bn of S&P next week in a flat tape and up to $65bn in a one-month downside scenario, against only $9bn of buying in the upside scenario.
Russell CTA positioning is the opposite: heavily short and potentially forced to buy on a rally. Russell rose about 2% while Nasdaq fell 70bps and SOX fell 3.2% on the day cited by Privorotsky.

Bond CTAs are short about $300bn in total (short $145mm DV01). The retrace lower in global yields, with 5.02% on the US 10-year as the key level, has created technical demand. In a flat one-week tape they cover $12bn DV01, and $25bn in an up tape. Over a month they cover $42bn DV01 in a flat tape and $165bn in an up tape.

Vol is starting to react. The Vol Panic Index rose from 4.63 on Wednesday to 7.94 on Friday, reaching the panic threshold for the first time since late July. The Nasdaq 100 one-week straddle is priced at 3% (about one-year high) and the S&P one-week straddle at 1.8% (about 60th percentile). VIX call vol shows extreme panic while S&P put vol is mid-percentile.

Trader fatigue is shown by the GS momentum factor basket (GSPRHIMO), which has had 30 daily moves of +/-5% in 2026. That is more than any year in the dataset including 2000 (23), 2008-09 (16) and 2020 (21). Cash and derivative volumes dried up into the weekend.

Garrett frames the market as either the 2nd inning of an AI ecosystem repricing or the 8th inning of a de-gross episode, and leans toward the latter. His conditions for the 8th-inning view are lower bond volatility, midterms out of the way, proof of AI capex payback in earnings, and oil below $90.

Pasquariello's S&P EPS growth estimates (ex-PE) are +29% in 2026, +18% in 2027 and +11% in 2028. He expects the primary trend to stay higher but with a flatter gradient: the bull market lives on but with less punch and more messiness.

Corporate credit has been weak and not limited to AI. Pasquariello says credit contacts described conditions as 'melting down'. He also notes S&P ex-AI is tracking for its best month in three years while AI leaders have fallen.

Event calendar is dense: Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday with the Fed decision, Amazon Thursday. 44% of S&P companies report EPS this week. Also UK Budget (possible bank taxes), China policy meetings, US 2/5/7-year supply, ECB and BOJ. The market expects the Fed to skip, and the question is whether Warsh focuses on hot inflation or on tighter financial conditions.

Brazil's presidential runoff: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to win, against prediction market expectations, with legal challenges looming. Privorotsky expects sizable pressure on Brazilian assets. The vol surface had priced a -22%/+13% asymmetric two-way move for the outcome.
Korea: KOSPI is down 40%. GS research cut its 12-month target from 12,000 to 9,000 but still sees over 60% upside, at 4x forward earnings with the memory cycle bad news priced in.

AAPL is negatively correlated to the Nasdaq 100 for the first time in history. The AI winners vs AI at risk pair is down 13% on the year, and S&P ex-AI has outperformed the S&P by 7.4% over three weeks.

vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund gross leverage 312% (96th percentile over 5 years), fundamental net leverage 47% (one-year low).
Fundamental net exposure at YTD lows with gross at 63rd percentile (Privorotsky). Net exposure is in the 0th percentile (Garrett).
Global tech selling was -3.3 sigma over two weeks, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4:1.
Thursday saw more tech selling than any other day in two years (GS PB).
TMT-focused hedge funds are down 9.6% MTD and Asia Fundamental L/S is down 9.3% MTD.
Fundamental L/S was -1.1% on the week, -3.8% MTD, +8.8% YTD (after a +17.4% June-quarter high). Systematic L/S was -2% on the week, its worst since 2024, -1.1% MTD, +18.7% YTD.
Equity CTAs are long $48bn of global stocks, almost all US, and sit on the medium-term thresholds in both S&P and Nasdaq 100, below which additional selling unlocks.
CTA flow model: sell $11.6bn S&P in a flat week, up to $65bn in a one-month downside scenario, only $9bn of buying in a one-month upside. Even a 2 SD rally leaves CTAs net sellers.
Vol Panic Index rose from 4.63 to 7.94. Downside skew and tails are outperforming, fixed-strike vol is bid, and VIX positioning is more prominent.
Nasdaq 100 one-week straddle at 3% (about one-year highs), S&P one-week straddle at 1.8% (about 60th percentile). Delta-adjusted VIX hit about one-year highs the prior Friday.
Brazil election vol surface implied a -22% / +13% two-way move, while no excess variance is priced in S&P or QQQ for the US midterms.
GSPESHRT (most vs least short in Europe) moved +3 standard deviations on a 60-day lookback.
geopolitical: Feared weekend escalation against Iran did not materialize, and diplomatic talks continue.
Privorotsky is confused by a policy that telegraphed escalation and let markets pre-price an energy shock, and suggests maximum pressure ahead of a possible last-minute grand bargain.
French protests were more contained than previous episodes and a downgrade was avoided.
Brazil's runoff: Lula won after overturning a first-round deficit, with legal challenges looming.
US midterms are creeping into client conversations and skew negative.
UK Budget risks include potential bank taxes.

tension_points.bull_case: Coppersmith and Pasquariello see a leverage unwind with intact demand, heavy de-risking, firmer implied vol and a negative Risk Appetite Indicator, which favors a relief rally if hyperscaler earnings cooperate. Garrett leans toward the 8th inning of de-grossing.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross leverage is still 96th percentile, CTAs hold $38.5bn long S&P with $65bn of modeled downside supply, and hyperscaler credit spreads have widened. Garrett's alternative is the 2nd inning of an AI repricing with material index catch-down.
tension_points.what_invalidates: S&P falling below the medium-term CTA trend threshold, about 1.3% below Friday's close, which unlocks additional systematic selling.

tension_points.bull_case: Capex rises alongside accelerating organic cash flow with a credible path to self-funding through 2027/28.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex accelerates on expensive debt, or is cut because financing is unavailable.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon guidance this week showing how capex is financed and how backlog converts to cloud revenue.
